related_questions.question: What is the best medicine to take for COVID symptoms?

text_blocks.snippet: For mild COVID-19 symptoms, over-the-counter medications like acetaminophen (Tylenol) or ibuprofen (Advil) can help manage fever, aches, and pains. If you have existing health problems, are over 65, or are immunocompromised, prescription medications may be more appropriate and should be discussed with a doctor immediately after testing positive, according to UChicago Medicine. Prescription treatments are most effective when started early in the course of the illness.

list.snippet: Over-the-counter medications: These can help relieve symptoms like fever, headache, and body aches.

Prescription medications: For those at higher risk, prescription medications like antivirals can shorten the duration and severity of the illness. These are most effective when started early after symptom onset, according to the Wisconsin Department of Health Services.

Consult a doctor: It's crucial to speak with a healthcare professional to determine the best course of treatment, especially if you have underlying health conditions or are at higher risk, says the CDC.

text_blocks.snippet: The fastest way to recover from COVID-19 symptoms depends on the severity of the illness. For mild cases, rest, hydration, and over-the-counter medications like acetaminophen or ibuprofen can help manage symptoms. For those at higher risk, early treatment with medications like Paxlovid is crucial and must be started within 5-7 days of symptom onset to be effective, according to the CDC.
